records.name: Archon
records.held_by: A harbour authority and merchant council in the East Empire Company's old buildings, with the successor state's customs officers alongside
records.summary: Archon is the province's best working harbour and its principal legal port, on the Padomaic coast where an estuary meets the sea. Amphibious civic life is ordinary here: children play underwater, guar breathe water, cargo moves above and below the surface. A sealed Shadowscale school stands closed in the town.

notes.text: A major port city on the eastern coast, marsh to the north and beaches to the south, beside an estuary that leads inland. It is the province's principal legal port and the south-east end of the Archon, Lilmoth, Soulrest and Tear trade line. Anyone arriving by sea or by the bayou channels passes through its harbour.

Founded as an Ayleid town by the Barsaebic exiles, on ground held earlier by the Lilmothiit and the Cantemiric Velothi. Its coast was full of pirates in the late First Era until General Lucinia Falco chartered them with letters of marque. The East Empire Company later ran its wharves, and the Shadowscales kept a school here that closed in 4E 187. Umbriel in 4E 48 never reached it.

In 4E 201 Archon is intact, busy and at ease with the successor state, which keeps customs officers in the port without trying to run it. The old Company wharves, bonded stores and counting-houses still stand and are used by the harbour authority, though the charter that built them is long dead.

About four in five are Argonians, with a sizeable Dunmer minority from Tear a short sail away, a few Imperials and Khajiit, and a floating population of sailors. Pilots, wharfingers, ferrymen and the merchant council hold the real authority.

The legal trade of the south-east: cargo handling, pilotage, bonded storage, ship chandlery, customs and the chartered privateers who stand in for a navy. Rice and fish arrive from the bayou by lighter; clay and dye come down from Aroxhu.

Sithis and the Hist as everywhere, but the nearest Hist is a small landward tree that harbour families tend; Imperial-descended residents keep a little of the Nine. Sailors leave offerings at the water stairs for those lost at sea.

A low harbour town of stone wharves and timber warehouses with Company brick at the waterfront, wooden stilt houses behind, and resort-style taverns whose balconies overlook the bay. Boats and swimmers fill the water; the sea smells of tar, salt and rotting weed.
Safe inside the walls; the harbour is policed and the water is a public road. Pickpockets, drunk sailors, and smugglers working the lower wharves are the usual trouble. Outside, the beaches are D1.

The sealed Shadowscale facility, which the Dark Brotherhood wants reopened and the city quietly watches, with a very old ku-vastei living near it. Paperwork disputes between chartered privateers and customs. Underwater games a visitor can join, which teach swimming before the deep water does.

records.name: Lilmoth
records.held_by: A reconstituted merchant council; no ruler
records.summary: Lilmoth is the Festering Jewel of Black Marsh, destroyed in 4E 48 and rebuilt smaller as a wholly Argonian stilt town over a mass grave. Its Old Imperial quarter lies drowned and unrepaired. A young Hist, feared and tended under a rotating guard of tree-minders, grows in the lower town.

notes.text: A merchant port on the southern point of the Althii islands, built over shallow water so large ships anchor out and lighter their goods in. It is the biggest town on the south coast and the market for the delta villages and estates of the Althii islands.

Founded by the Lilmothiit, ruled by Priest-Kings, taken by the Empire, then wrested back by the An-Xileel before 4E 48. Its second Hist went mad and summoned Umbriel in 4E 48, and the Slaughter at Lilmoth destroyed the city. The site was resettled within generations because the harbour has no rival nearby.

Rebuilt but not restored: smaller, lower, and wholly Argonian in its fabric. The merchant council sets tariffs and pays guards. It is hostile to the successor state, which was the party that killed it, and the old law keeping unlicensed foreigners on the docks lapses in places and is enforced in others.

About four in five are Argonians, with a working foreign dock population of Bretons, Khajiit and Imperial-descended traders. Elders, including retired Shadowscales, settle disputes. Tree-minders rotate through the Hist's post so that no one holds it alone.
Lighterage, bay trade, salvage from the drowned quarter, and rice from Hereguard-style plantations nearby. Pusbottom, repopulated as slums always are, supplies the criminal trade of the coast.

The third Hist is walled but open, tended by two minders at once, and no faction may hold exclusive access. A sunken shrine to Xhon-Mehl the Fisher, the Ancestral Organ Lord of Lilmoth, is known to divers.

Ninety percent of the fabric is Argonian stilts and platforms that climb into the air, wired together by walkways, over a drowned layer of Imperial villas. Old Imperial walls survive in places; mould, vines, big bamboo, sleeping palms and harmless drifting shines mark the drowned quarter.

The town centre is D1: guarded by the council's men, with ripper eels in the canals and cutpurses in Pusbottom. The drowned Imperial quarter and the Hist's roots are D3, with sea-drakes in the deep water beyond.

The unnamed name of the drowned quarter, which locals will not say to strangers. The third Hist and the rule written around it. Pusbottom's criminal quarter and the lapsed docks-only law. Salvage from the drowned villas, and the sunken shrine of Xhon-Mehl.

records.name: Uluo
records.held_by: The elder of the Three Waters Tribe and the tribe's council of raft-masters
records.summary: Uluo is the one town of the Three Waters Tribe, on the north shore of the Althii islands facing the Nushara Bayou. It is the seat of the tribe's elder and the market where the bayou hamlets sell rice, shellfish and reed. The tribe deals with Archon as an equal and with Lilmoth by the back-water routes.

notes.text: The one town of the Three Waters Tribe, and the place the bayou hamlets send their catch, rice and reed. It matters as the tribe's seat and as a crossing point between Archon, Lilmoth and the Nushara waters.

notes.text: Canon records only that the tribe's Elder Nuetepa was active in Archon in the Second Era. The tribe's first settlement on the islands is unrecorded; the town grew where the bayou channels meet the open strait, safe from the flu that emptied the coast of other peoples.

A market town of raft-houses and stilt halls, never taken by any power and untouched by Umbriel. The tribe is wary of the An-Xileel's successors and sends its own to sit with Archon's merchants, so it is both neutral ground and a smuggler's door.

Three Waters Argonians, the elder, a council of raft-masters who keep the channel routes, a handful of Archon and Lilmoth factors, and traders from Aroxhu. Population at the town tier, about two dozen households' worth of named people.
Net-fish, shellfish, saltrice, reed mats and bundles, and the back-water freight that moves between Archon and the Lilmoth delta without passing customs. The elder takes a share of every raft.
Argonian Sithis and Hist devotion; the town keeps a small Hist pool tended by a tree-minder, and hatching families come in from the hamlets. Rafts are blessed at launching.
A pentagon of raft-mounted halls and reed houses around a landing, with a long communal hall for the elder's moot, drying frames of fish, and rafts lashed in rings that shift with the channels.
Safe in the town. The channels around it hold slaughterfish, ripper eels and the odd smuggler who has not paid the elder's share.
An elder's request to carry a message or cargo to Archon unseen. A raft-master with a map of channels the customs men do not know. A dispute over the Hist pool's tending.
